content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text labels Matthew 1:16 UNDERDETERMINED because a single verse admits both readings, which is the kind of single-verse/openness ground the rule governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"\"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.\" I weighed reading it as making a two-sense verse open/UNDERDETERMINED versus reading it as requiring both senses to stand and forbidding UNDERDETERMINED on that basis.","why":"The rule says a two-sense verse is not open and both senses stand, but the judge used Matthew 1:16's admitted two readings as the ground for UNDERDETERMINED."}
